# Adjudication Task — Chapter 396

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃396화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|검은 기사는 고개를 들어 하늘을 올려다보았다.
  6|
  7|구름 한 점 없이 푸르른 창공. 그러나 이미 빛을 잃은 검은 기사의 눈에는 어둡고 탁한 잿빛으로 보일 뿐이었다.
  8|
  9|‘어둡구나.’
 10|
 11|문득 떠오른 생각에 검은 기사는 기분이 이상해졌다. 어둡다니. 도대체 어둠이 무엇을 뜻한단 말인가.
 12|
 13|처음부터 그는 검은 기사였다. 어둠에서 태어난 존재는 어둠이라는 의미를 모른다.
 14|
 15|‘하지만 이건. 뭐지?’
 16|
 17|빛과 햇살. 맑게 웃는 아이. 자신의 머리를 쓰다듬는 누군가의 손길…….
 18|
 19|연달아 뇌리를 스치는 여러 단어와 알 수 없는 장면들이 그를 혼란스럽게 만들었다.
 20|
 21|다음 순간 들려온 수하의 부름이 아니었다면, 검은 기사는 한참을 그렇게 서 있었을 것이다.
 22|
 23|- 로드.
 24|
 25|- 부디.
 26|
 27|전신을 감싼 칠흑 같은 갑주. 머리 전체를 덮은 투구 사이로 녹색 안광이 일렁인다.
 28|
 29|해골마에서 내려 한쪽 무릎을 꿇은 두 기의 데스나이트가 고저 없는 목소리로 말을 이었다.
 30|
 31|- 명령을.
 32|
 33|- 내려 주십시오.
 34|
 35|아.
 36|
 37|검은 기사는 잠시 잊고 있던 사실을 떠올렸다. 그것은 그가 모시는 군주가 내린 명령이었다.
 38|
 39|- 가라. 사방으로 진격하여 모든 것을 짓밟고 죽여라. 시체의 산과 피의 바다를 내게 바쳐라.
 40|
 41|군주의 명령은 절대적이다. 그에게 영혼까지 종속된 검은 기사는 충실히 명령을 따랐다.
 42|
 43|휘하에 놓인 열 기의 데스나이트를 다섯 군단의 사령관으로 삼고, 스스로 한 군단의 선봉장이 되어 이곳에 왔다.
 44|
 45|‘그런데 왜 하필 이곳일까.’
 46|
 47|검은 기사는 저 멀리 보이는 작은 도시를 바라보았다.
 48|
 49|기억에 있는 장소다. ‘아이’라는 낯선 단어를 불현듯 떠올린 곳이었고, 정체 모를 거대한 힘을 느낀 곳이기도 했다.
 50|
 51|하지만 도대체 어떤 이유로 자신이 이곳으로 향했는지, 검은 기사는 알지 못했다.
 52|
 53|- 로드?
 54|
 55|- 로드?
 56|
 57|수하들을 가만히 내려다보던 검은 기사는 마침내 명했다.
 58|
 59|- 진격하라.
 60|
 61|- 명을.
 62|
 63|- 받듭니다.
 64|
 65|기다리던 대답을 들은 데스나이트가 해골마에 올라 거대한 창을 번쩍 치켜들었다.
 66|
 67|창날에서 솟구친 칠흑색의 마기(魔氣)에 너른 평야를 빽빽하게 메운 몬스터들이 괴성을 내질렀다.
 68|
 69|- 끽. 끼기기긱.
 70|
 71|- 그어어어어!
 72|
 73|죽은 지 얼마 되지 않아 아직 살점이 붙어 있는 스켈레톤부터 소형 몬스터인 고블린, 오크. 트롤과 오우거 등의 대형 몬스터까지.
 74|
 75|그 숫자가 어림잡아 수만을 헤아렸고 상공에는 가고일과 와이번 무리가 거대한 그림자를 드리웠다.
 76|
 77|- 집결.
 78|
 79|- 하라.
 80|
 81|이어지는 지시에 이백여 기의 듀라한(Dullahan)이 정렬했다. 한 손에는 자신의 잘려 나간 머리를, 다른 한 손에는 무기를 든 그들은 백골로 이루어진 짐승 위에 올라 흉광을 번뜩였다.
 82|
 83|- 돌격.
 84|
 85|- 준비.
 86|
 87|두 기의 데스나이트가 군단의 꼭짓점이 되었다. 하늘을 찌를 듯이 높이 솟구친 창날이 천천히 내려가 도시를 겨누었다.
 88|
 89|인간들의 도시. 그러나 이제 곧 언데드의 도시이자 죽음의 땅이 될 곳이다.
 90|
 91|「공안무력부는 집결하라!」
 92|
 93|「씨, 씨발! 몬스터들이다! 놈들이 나타났다!」
 94|
 95|「당장 경보를 울리고 사령부에 보고해!」
 96|
 97|위이이이잉!
 98|
 99|불어오는 바람을 타고 인간들의 외침과 비상을 알리는 소리가 울려 퍼졌다.
100|
101|그러나 이미 명령은 떨어졌다. 진격을 시작한 언데드 군단을 멈출 수 있는 건 아무것도 없었다.
102|
103|쿵, 쿵, 쿵.
104|
105|칼같이 짜인 오와 열.
106|
107|데스나이트와 듀라한을 필두로 빠른 기동력을 갖춘 라이칸스로프 등이 최전방에 섰고 오우거와 트롤, 골렘과 같은 대형 몬스터가 거대한 벽이 되어 이동했다.
108|
109|활과 마법을 다루는 몬스터는 최후방으로 이동한 지 오래.
110|
111|일반 몬스터들에게는 없는 규율과 대형을 생각해 낸 것 역시 검은 기사였다.
112|
113|‘나는 도대체 어디서 이런 것을 배웠던가.’
114|
115|다시금 떠오른 의문을 뒤로하고 검은 기사는 입을 열었다.
116|
117|- 따르라.
118|
119|주인의 뜻에 따라, 그가 탄 해골마가 걸음을 옮기기 시작한다.
120|
121|다그닥, 다그닥.
122|
123|백골로 이루어진 말발굽이 새싹을 짓밟았다. 드넓은 곡창(穀倉)을 뒤덮은 언데드 군단이 자신들의 사령관을 따라 천천히 진격한다.
124|
125|거대한 진동이 지축을 울리고, 느린 물결처럼 나아가던 군단은 이내 백골의 파도가 되어 평야를 휩쓸었다.
126|
127|두두두두두두!
128|
129|- 그아아아아아!
130|
131|수만의 몬스터가 토해 내는 거대한 함성.
132|
133|도시를 향해 밀려드는 몬스터들의 선두에, 한 줄기 빛이 되어 쏘아지는 검은 기사가 있었다.
134|
135|「저놈이 우두머리다!」
136|
137|「원거리 부대! 준비!」
138|
139|「탱커들은 동요하지 마라! 전차 부대는 헌터들과 함께 놈을 요격해라!」
140|
141|탱커, 전차, 헌터.
142|
143|검은 기사는 인간들의 외침을 들을 수 있었고, 놀랍게도 정확히 이해했다.
144|
145|심지어는 그 뒤에 나올 명령까지도.
146|
147|「집중 사격 개시!」
148|
149|타다다다당!
150|
151|퍼버버버벙!
152|
153|쉬쉬쉬쉬쉭!
154|
155|화려하다. 불꽃이, 얼음이, 섬광이 도시 곳곳에서 솟구친다.
156|
157|더러는 곡선을 그리며 내리꽂혔고, 더러는 일직선에 가까운 궤적으로 검은 기사와 그의 뒤를 따르는 언데드 기사단을 노렸다.
158|
159|- 아아.
160|
161|잿빛으로 물든 세상에서도 그것들이 뿜어내는 빛은 매혹적이었고 친숙했다. 검은 기사는 왠지 모를 울렁임을 느끼며 손을 뻗었다.
162|
163|스르릉.
164|
165|등에 매여 있던 대검이 뽑혀 나온다.
166|
167|발사된 포탄과 마법, 화살이 그에게 닿기도 전, 칠흑빛을 띤 검신이 허공을 종횡(縱橫)으로 긋고 베었다.
168|
169|콰아아아아!
170|
171|마력의 바람이 휘몰아친다. 공간이 갈라진다. 휘황찬란한 마나를 머금은 마법이 촛불처럼 꺼지고 화살은 산산이 부서졌다.
172|
173|빛이 어둠에 잡아먹히는 광경을, 도시에 있던 모두는 똑똑히 지켜보았다.
174|
175|최민우와 샤오 쉔의 뇌리에 한 가지 생각이 스쳐 지나갔다.
176|
177|‘이건…….’
178|
179|‘막을 수 없다.’
180|
181|확신에 가까운 깨달음. 그리고 다음 순간 공간을 뛰어넘어 헌터들을 향해 들이닥친 칠흑빛 섬광.
182|
183|콰아아아앙!
184|
185|하늘이 쪼개지는 듯한 굉음이 울려 퍼졌다.
186|
187|수십 개의 타워 실드가 박살 나고 피 보라가 터져 나온다. 일검(一劍)을 휘둘러 세 명의 A급 헌터와 스무 명의 B급 헌터를 베어 버린 검은 기사는 붉은 안광으로 얼어붙은 인간들을 바라보았다.
188|
189|깊숙이 눌러쓴 투구 아래로, 스산한 망자의 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
190|
191|- 악사르. 가로쉬.
192|
193|모두 죽여라.
194|
195|전날 이곳에서 죽어 갔던 이들이 마지막으로 들었던 마계의 언어.
196|
197|그리고…… 검은 기사가 자신의 뒤를 따른 군단을 향해 내린 명령.
198|
199|- 명을.
200|
201|- 받듭니다.
202|
203|검은 기사의 좌우로 모습을 드러낸 두 기의 데스나이트, 이어 들이닥친 일백의 듀라한이 예리한 송곳이 되어 인(人)의 장벽을 꿰뚫었다.
204|
205|콰드드드득!
206|
207|
208|
209|* * *
210|
211|
212|
213|‘기습이라고?’
214|
215|각 전선에서 올라온 긴급 보고. 웨이펑후가 어떻게 된 일이냐며 호통을 쳤지만, 돌아온 건 각 전선과 통신이 완전히 두절되었다는 소식이었다.
216|
217|「완전 두절이라니! 어젯밤부터는 불안정하긴 해도 연결은 되지 않았나!」
218|
219|통신 장교가 식은땀을 흘리며 대답했다.
220|
221|「그, 그게…… 어떤 이유에서인지 통신 방해가 더욱 강해졌습니다. 막 도착한 긴급 보고도 약 30분 전의 것으로 확인되었습니다.」
222|
223|“……!”
224|
225|뭐? 삼십 분?
226|
227|저 말이 사실이라면 회의 진행 도중 습격이 이루어졌다는 뜻이다.
228|
229|그마저도 통신 방해에 헤매다가 겨우 도착한 소식이니, 30분이 아니라 한 시간일 수도 있다.
230|
231|매직 존슨의 얼굴이 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴로 중얼거렸다.
232|
233|「그럴 리가. 분명 내가 가기 전만 해도 그 정도는…….」
234|
235|문득 도시를 떠나기 전, 매직 존슨이 했던 말이 뇌리를 스쳤다.
236|
237|
238|
239|‘아크 리치. 놈의 힘이 아주 조금씩 줄어들고 있어. 특히 어젯밤을 기점으로 방해 요소가 상당 부분 사라지게 되었지.’
240|
241|
242|
243|틀렸다.
244|
245|인근에 미치는 아크 리치의 힘이 약화 된 것이 아니라, 놈이 그렇게 보이게끔 만든 것이다.
246|
247|티 내지 않고 조금씩. 그러다가 군단을 물림으로써 마치 자신의 힘이 미치는 범위가 대폭 줄어든 것처럼. 우리가 조금이라도 더 안심할 수 있게끔.
248|
249|‘이건…….’
250|
251|철저한 함정이다.
252|
253|아크 리치가 S급 헌터들의 부재를 어떻게 알아차렸는지는 모른다. 중요한 것은 놈이 그 짧은 틈을 포착하여 몬스터 군단을 진격시켰다는 것이다.
254|
255|전날에 목격했던 참혹한 도륙이 전선 곳곳에서 벌어진다고 생각하니, 처음 텔레포트를 겪었을 때보다 더한 울렁거림이 찾아왔다.
256|
257|하지만 이번에는 구역질 대신 매직 존슨을 붙잡고 말했다.
258|
259|“텔레포트.”
260|
261|「뭐?」
262|
263|“텔레포트요. 어서!”
264|
265|나는 매직 존슨이 당장이라도 마법을 써 줄 줄 알았다. 그러나 다음 순간 들려온 그의 대답은 내가 생각했던 것이 아니었다.
266|
267|「진. 제트기를 타고 가.」
268|
269|“네? 제트기라니 갑자기 그게 무슨……. 그럼 너무 늦어요.”
270|
271|「지금은 곤란해.」
272|
273|“어째서입니까? 아까 우리가 있던 병원 옥상 좌표, 알고 있잖아요.”
274|
275|매직 존슨이 고개를 저었다.
276|
277|「좌표가 문제가 아니야. 이대로 텔레포트를 시도한다면…… 우리 둘 다 죽을 수도 있어.」
278|
279|“……!”
280|
281|다급함에 잠시 잊고 있었다. 아크 리치의 마법 방해에 대해서. 이런 함정을 판 놈이 친절하게 텔레포트를 시도하게 둘 리 없다.
282|
283|매직 존슨이 가라앉은 목소리로 말을 이었다.
284|
285|「십 분. 길어야 이십 분이야. 제트기를 타, 진.」
286|
287|“……그사이에 많은 사람이 죽을 겁니다.”
288|
289|「그래. 하지만 텔레포트를 하는 과정에서 네가 개죽음을 당한다면, 더 많은 사상자가 나오겠지.」
290|
291|S급 헌터는 전세를 뒤엎을 수 있는 전략 병기다.
292|
293|늦더라도 도착만 한다면 일부를 살릴 수 있겠지만, 텔레포트 과정에서 사고라도 난다면 나와 지원군을 잃은 수많은 사람은 함께 돌아올 수 없는 강을 건너게 될 것이다.
294|
295|지금 매직 존슨은 나를 걱정하는 동시에 그 점을 지적하고 있었다.
296|
297|「용감하지만, 어리석은 짓이야.」
298|
299|“…….”
300|
301|「곧 제트기가 이륙 준비를 끝마칠 거야. 이럴 시간 없어.」
302|
303|대회의실의 한 면을 차지한 방탄 유리창 밖으로 이륙장을 가로질러 기체에 탑승하는 파일럿들이 보인다.
304|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

Emergency reports had come in from every front. Wei Fenghu roared, demanding to know what had happened, but the only answer he received was that communications with every front had been completely severed.

[P108]
“Completely severed? They may have been unstable, but haven’t we still been able to connect since last night?”

[P109]
The communications officer answered, drenched in cold sweat.

[P110]
“W-we don’t know why, but the interference has grown even stronger. The emergency report that just arrived appears to have been sent approximately thirty minutes ago.”

[P111]
“……!”

[P112]
What? Thirty minutes?

[P113]
If that was true, the attacks had begun while the meeting was in progress.

[P114]
And since the report had barely made it through the interference, it might not have been thirty minutes ago. It could have been an hour.

[P115]
Magic Johnson’s face went rigid.

[P116]
“That can’t be. It wasn’t nearly this bad before I left…”

[P117]
The words he had spoken before leaving the city suddenly flashed through my mind.

[P118]
*“The Arch Lich’s power is gradually weakening. A considerable portion of the interference has disappeared since last night in particular.”*

[P119]
Wrong.

[P120]
The Arch Lich’s power over the surrounding area hadn’t weakened. It had merely made it look that way.

[P121]
Little by little, without giving anything away. Then it withdrew its legions, making it seem as though the range of its power had shrunk dramatically—all so we would let our guard down, even if only a little.

[P122]
*This is…*

[P123]
A meticulously laid trap.

[P124]
I didn’t know how the Arch Lich had realized the S-rank Hunters were gone. What mattered was that it had seized that brief opening and sent the monster legions forward.

[P125]
The thought of the horrific slaughter we had witnessed the day before now unfolding across every front made my stomach churn even worse than it had during my first teleportation.

[P126]
But this time, instead of throwing up, I grabbed Magic Johnson.

[P127]
“Teleport.”

[P128]
“What?”

[P129]
“Teleport. Hurry!”

[P130]
I expected Magic Johnson to use magic immediately. But his answer was nothing like what I had expected.

[P131]
“Jin. Take a jet.”

[P132]
“What? A jet? Why are you suddenly…? We’ll be too late.”

[P133]
“It’s too risky right now.”

[P134]
“Why? You know the coordinates of the hospital rooftop where we were earlier.”

[P135]
Magic Johnson shook his head.

[P136]
“The coordinates aren’t the problem. If we attempt to teleport like this…we could both die.”

[P137]
“……!”

[P138]
In my desperation, I had momentarily forgotten about the Arch Lich’s magical interference. There was no way the bastard who had laid such a trap would kindly allow us to teleport.

[P139]
Magic Johnson continued in a subdued voice.

[P140]
“Ten minutes. Twenty at most. Take the jet, Jin.”

[P141]
“……A lot of people will die in that time.”

[P142]
“Yes. But if you get yourself killed for nothing during the teleportation, there’ll be even more casualties.”

[P143]
An S-rank Hunter was a strategic weapon capable of turning the tide of a war.

[P144]
Even if I arrived late, I might still be able to save some people. But if something went wrong during the teleportation, there would be no saving me or the countless people left without reinforcements.

[P145]
Magic Johnson was worried about me, but he was also pointing that out.

[P146]
“It’s brave, but foolish.”

[P147]
“……”

[P148]
“The jet will be ready for takeoff soon. We don’t have time for this.”

[P149]
Through the bulletproof glass covering one wall of the conference room, I could see pilots crossing the runway and boarding their aircraft.

[P150]
I could also see the backs of the other S-rank Hunters, who had already left the conference room.

[P151]
I watched in silence, then suddenly spoke.

[P152]
“You said it was possible, right?”

[P153]
“What?”

[P154]
“Teleporting missiles, like in the hologram footage we saw earlier.”

[P155]
Magic Johnson’s eyes widened.

[P156]
“Jin, don’t tell me…”

[P157]
“There’s no need for you to risk yourself too, Johnson. Sending me alone will be enough.”

[P158]
“Good God. Are you crazy? I explained it to you, and you still don’t understand!”

[P159]
“I understand perfectly. I’m prepared to take that risk.”

[P160]
“You…”

[P161]
His lips moved as though he were about to say something, but then he suddenly slammed his fist down on the table.

[P162]
Bang!

[P163]
The expensive hardwood shattered beneath the force of his blow.

[P164]
“Damn it! Fuck this whole goddamn mess!”

[P165]
I let out a quiet laugh as I watched Magic Johnson mutter curse after curse.

[P166]
I already knew what his reaction meant.

[P167]
“I can take that as permission, right?”

[P168]
“Yes, you insolent little brat.”

[P169]
His bloodshot eyes fixed on me.

[P170]
He looked ready to unleash another torrent of abuse.

[P171]
Magic Johnson was genuinely furious—and at the same time, deeply saddened.

[P172]
“Listen, Jin. I…”

[P173]
“I know. You have people you need to protect too. I’m sorry to ask this of you.”

[P174]
“……Damn it. The hospital rooftop, right?”

[P175]
“Yes. That’s enough.”

[P176]
Swoosh.

[P177]
Magic Johnson clenched his teeth and pressed his thick palm against my chest.

[P178]
As though taking every possible precaution, his mana slowly began to envelop my body, unlike the first time he had teleported me.

[P179]
“Ten percent. Those are your odds of survival. There’s a ninety percent chance you’ll die.”

[P180]
Ten percent…

[P181]
I raised my head and looked at the sky beyond the window.

[P182]
A clear blue expanse without a single cloud. Was Murim somewhere in the distant universe beyond that sky? Were they waiting for me?

[P183]
At that moment, a thought suddenly occurred to me, and the corners of my mouth lifted.

[P184]
“That’s not bad. Ten percent is enough.”

[P185]
“What?”

[P186]
A dazzling mass of light burst forth. Feeling warmth envelop my entire body, I continued.

[P187]
“It’s probably a thousand times higher than the odds of crossing dimensions.”

[P188]
“……!”

[P189]
I wondered what expression Magic Johnson was wearing by then.

[P190]
I wanted to know, but unfortunately, I could no longer see his face. A blinding flash filled my vision, and a rough, powerful force sucked me through the warping space.

[P191]
Whoooosh!

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 396

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃396화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|검은 기사는 고개를 들어 하늘을 올려다보았다.
  6|
  7|구름 한 점 없이 푸르른 창공. 그러나 이미 빛을 잃은 검은 기사의 눈에는 어둡고 탁한 잿빛으로 보일 뿐이었다.
  8|
  9|‘어둡구나.’
 10|
 11|문득 떠오른 생각에 검은 기사는 기분이 이상해졌다. 어둡다니. 도대체 어둠이 무엇을 뜻한단 말인가.
 12|
 13|처음부터 그는 검은 기사였다. 어둠에서 태어난 존재는 어둠이라는 의미를 모른다.
 14|
 15|‘하지만 이건. 뭐지?’
 16|
 17|빛과 햇살. 맑게 웃는 아이. 자신의 머리를 쓰다듬는 누군가의 손길…….
 18|
 19|연달아 뇌리를 스치는 여러 단어와 알 수 없는 장면들이 그를 혼란스럽게 만들었다.
 20|
 21|다음 순간 들려온 수하의 부름이 아니었다면, 검은 기사는 한참을 그렇게 서 있었을 것이다.
 22|
 23|- 로드.
 24|
 25|- 부디.
 26|
 27|전신을 감싼 칠흑 같은 갑주. 머리 전체를 덮은 투구 사이로 녹색 안광이 일렁인다.
 28|
 29|해골마에서 내려 한쪽 무릎을 꿇은 두 기의 데스나이트가 고저 없는 목소리로 말을 이었다.
 30|
 31|- 명령을.
 32|
 33|- 내려 주십시오.
 34|
 35|아.
 36|
 37|검은 기사는 잠시 잊고 있던 사실을 떠올렸다. 그것은 그가 모시는 군주가 내린 명령이었다.
 38|
 39|- 가라. 사방으로 진격하여 모든 것을 짓밟고 죽여라. 시체의 산과 피의 바다를 내게 바쳐라.
 40|
 41|군주의 명령은 절대적이다. 그에게 영혼까지 종속된 검은 기사는 충실히 명령을 따랐다.
 42|
 43|휘하에 놓인 열 기의 데스나이트를 다섯 군단의 사령관으로 삼고, 스스로 한 군단의 선봉장이 되어 이곳에 왔다.
 44|
 45|‘그런데 왜 하필 이곳일까.’
 46|
 47|검은 기사는 저 멀리 보이는 작은 도시를 바라보았다.
 48|

[P132]
“What? A jet? Why are you suddenly…? We’ll be too late.”

[P133]
“It’s too risky right now.”

[P134]
“Why? You know the coordinates of the hospital rooftop where we were earlier.”

[P135]
Magic Johnson shook his head.

[P136]
“The coordinates aren’t the problem. If we attempt to teleport like this…we could both die.”

[P137]
“……!”

[P138]
In my desperation, I had momentarily forgotten about the Arch Lich’s magical interference. There was no way the bastard who had laid such a trap would kindly allow us to teleport.

[P139]
Magic Johnson continued in a subdued voice.

[P140]
“Ten minutes. Twenty at most. Take the jet, Jin.”

[P141]
“……A lot of people will die in that time.”

[P142]
“Yes. But if you get yourself killed for nothing during the teleportation, there’ll be even more casualties.”

[P143]
An S-rank Hunter was a strategic weapon capable of turning the tide of a war.

[P144]
Even if I arrived late, I might still be able to save some people. But if something went wrong during the teleportation, there would be no saving me or the countless people left without reinforcements.

[P145]
Magic Johnson was worried about me, but he was also pointing that out.

[P146]
“It’s brave, but foolish.”

[P147]
“……”

[P148]
“The jet will be ready for takeoff soon. We don’t have time for this.”

[P149]
Through the bulletproof glass covering one wall of the conference room, I could see pilots crossing the runway and boarding their aircraft.

[P150]
I could also see the backs of the other S-rank Hunters, who had already left the conference room.

[P151]
I watched in silence, then suddenly spoke.

[P152]
“You said it was possible, right?”

[P153]
“What?”

[P154]

[P155]
Magic Johnson’s eyes widened.

[P156]
“Jin, don’t tell me…”

[P157]
“There’s no need for you to risk yourself too, Johnson. Sending me alone will be enough.”

[P158]
“Good God. Are you crazy? I explained it to you, and you still don’t understand!”

[P159]
“I understand perfectly. I’m prepared to take that risk.”

[P160]
“You…”

[P161]
His lips moved as though he were about to say something, but then he suddenly slammed his fist down on the table.

[P162]
Bang!

[P163]
The expensive hardwood shattered beneath the force of his blow.

[P164]
“Damn it! Fuck this whole goddamn mess!”

[P165]
I let out a quiet laugh as I watched Magic Johnson mutter curse after curse.

[P166]
I already knew what his reaction meant.

[P167]
“I can take that as permission, right?”

[P168]
“Yes, you insolent little brat.”

[P169]
His bloodshot eyes fixed on me.

[P170]
He looked ready to unleash another torrent of abuse.

[P171]
Magic Johnson was genuinely furious—and at the same time, deeply saddened.

[P172]
“Listen, Jin. I…”

[P173]
“I know. You have people you need to protect too. I’m sorry to ask this of you.”

[P174]
“……Damn it. The hospital rooftop, right?”

[P175]
“Yes. That’s enough.”

[P176]
Swoosh.

[P177]
Magic Johnson clenched his teeth and pressed his thick palm against my chest.

[P178]
As though taking every possible precaution, his mana slowly began to envelop my body, unlike the first time he had teleported me.

[P179]
“Ten percent. Those are your odds of survival. There’s a ninety percent chance you’ll die.”

[P180]
Ten percent…

[P181]
I raised my head and looked at the sky beyond the window.

[P182]
A clear blue expanse without a single cloud. Was Murim somewhere in the distant universe beyond that sky? Were they waiting for me?

[P183]
At that moment, a thought suddenly occurred to me, and the corners of my mouth lifted.

[P184]
“That’s not bad. Ten percent is enough.”

[P185]
“What?”

[P186]
A dazzling mass of light burst forth. Feeling warmth envelop my entire body, I continued.

[P187]
“It’s probably a thousand times higher than the odds of crossing dimensions.”

[P188]
“……!”

[P189]
I wondered what expression Magic Johnson was wearing by then.

[P190]

[P191]
Whoooosh!

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.
